findings.statement: the store is larger than the memory allowed to cache it
the default readahead does not amplify a random read
findings.detail: 12019153 device bytes per 100-byte value with the default advice against 8565 with MADV_RANDOM -- 120191.5x against 85.6x amplification. Measured from /proc/self/io with the page cache dropped first, so these are bytes the device was asked for and not bytes inferred from file size

findings.statement: telling the kernel a random read is random makes it faster
findings.detail: 6212 reads/s with MADV_RANDOM against 176 with the default (random vs default: greater 35.204x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 46.8%/10.4%)). Major faults: 4182 against 4284 -- the proof that these passes were cold, and the count of times the engine stopped for the disk

notes: page cache dropped before every pass; read amplification measured from /proc/self/io rather than inferred. Both arms read the same file in the same process and differ only in ReadOptions::readahead
